To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

four weeks of supplementation with red pepper spice (1 g/day) and turmeric powder (2.8 g/day) in a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, crossover design in 62 overweight and obese females did not significantly alter inflammation or oxidative stress biomarkers or global metabolic profile.

4-week dietary supplementation with red pepper spice or turmeric at levels used in foods did not alter inflammation or oxidative stress biomarkers in overweight/obesity females with systemic inflammation.

four-week supplementation with red pepper spice (1 g/day) or turmeric (2.8 g/day) did not significantly alter inflammation or oxidative stress biomarkers, or the global metabolic profile of overweight/obese women with systemic inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of RP and TM to alter oxidative stress and inflammation in overweight/ obese females with systemic inflammation.
the effects of red pepper and turmeric supplementation on biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative status in overweight females with systemic inflammation.

the influence of red pepper spice (RP, 1 g/d for 4 weeks) and turmeric spice (TM, 2.8 mg/d for 4 weeks) on oxidative stress, inflammation, and metabolic profiles of overweight/obese women with systemic inflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

4-week consumption of RP or TM at levels used in culinary applications does not significantly influence inflammation, oxidative stress, or metabolic profile in overweight females with systemic inflammation.

4-weeks supplementation with either red pepper spice or turmeric did not alter the global metabolic profile, oxidative stress, or inflammation in this group of overweight/obese individuals with systemic inflammation.

4-week consumption of RP or TM at the levels tested did not influence oxidative stress or inflammation, and did not alter the global metabolic profile of overweight/obese women with elevated systemic inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RP and TM are unlikely to be useful as dietary supplements to improve inflammation or oxidative stress in overweight/obesity.
4-week consumption of RP or TM at a culinary level does not alter inflammation, oxidative stress, or global metabolic profile in overweight/obesity females.
4-weeks supplementation with red pepper or turmeric at culinary levels does influence neither the oxidative stress nor the inflammation in overweight females with systemic inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RP or TM supplementation at the levels tested does not alter the inflammatory status or the metabolic profile of overweight/obese individuals with systemic inflammation.

the use of RP or TM as a flavoring in foods or for medicinal purposes does not appear to alter inflammation or oxidative stress, or cause a global metabolic shift in overweight/obse females with systemic inflammation.
the use of RP and TM at culinary levels in overweight and obese individuals does not appear to influence systemic inflammation or oxidative stress.
